blocks.text: The opening

**This is the Tilde Card: a business card you print yourself.** Scan its code and your website opens. Tap it and the phone gets whatever you wrote to the NFC sticker inside: your link, or your whole contact card if it fits. The box only holds a few, so here’s every design.
How it works

items.text: **Scan it.** The QR code on the front opens your link, up to 53 characters, in any phone’s camera.
**Tap it.** With an NFC sticker inside, iPhones and Android phones with NFC open your link from a tap, and they don’t need an app. (Older iPhones need the NFC reader in Control Center.)
**Free and open source.** The model is free to download, print and change. Its source is MIT-licensed, and the printable files on MakerWorld are CC BY 4.0. `[depends on U3]` for “on MakerWorld”.
**You print it yourself,** all at once, on a multi-color printer such as a Bambu Lab printer with an AMS or AMS lite.

blocks.text: Scanned or tapped

head: What the other phone gets
rows: Your link, from the code printed on the front. It’s printed for good, so it can’t change.
Whatever you wrote to the sticker: a link, or your whole contact card if it fits. A phone rewrites the sticker, so you can change it later without a reprint.
It has no code. A tap is all it does.

blocks.text: **A contact card on the sticker:** Android offers to save it if your card fits. An NTAG215 sticker holds 504 bytes, so a card with several links needs an NTAG216. A full card that doesn’t fit is written as its contact link, which opens your contact page and needs internet. `[depends on 1.3.0, T1–T4]` for the contact link. Tilde’s Write a sticker tells you which sizes fit before it writes. `[depends on T-W1–T-W7]` On an iPhone, a tap opens a page with your card and **Save contact**, which needs internet. `[depends on T1–T4]` for the iPhone line.

Fronts `[depends on the card release]`
Seven front styles. The lineup shows mostly **Classic**: your handle, your name, your website and the code.

items.text: **Minimal:** your name, larger, and the code.
**Mystery:** only the code, in the middle. With a smaller code, your handle sits at the top left.
**Handle:** your `~/handle`, large, and the code.
**Badge:** your first name, large, with your last name, your role and the code.
**Tap only:** your name and large tap waves, with no code.
**Blank:** nothing printed at all.

blocks.text: The code comes in three sizes: Full, Medium and Small.
one card in each front style
Backs

items.text: **Terminal window:** a `$` command, such as `$ whoami`, and your three lines.
**Plain:** your lines.
**Contact:** your lines, with icons (phone, email, web and more). `[depends on the card release]`
**Code:** your lines as a short JSON-style block. `[depends on the card release]`
**None:** plain, and the quickest to print.

blocks.text: **Alternate backs** swap a design’s colors, or swap its text for a tap mark. The lineup has 23. They include: `[depends on the card release]`

blocks.text: the alternate backs, each beside its design's default back
Two-piece or solid `[depends on two-piece card]`

items.text: **Two-piece** (the default): the card prints as two pieces, side by side and face down, so both faces come out smooth and matte. There’s no pause. Stick the NFC sticker into the front piece, then press the back piece in: it clicks past a lip and sits flush.
sub: **Unglued, it holds,** and the back lifts out at a corner with a fingernail, so you can swap the sticker.
**Glued** with superglue gel, it’s permanent: the most durable card.
**Mix and match:** a back fits any front printed with the same settings (the same sticker and the same edge marks), so one card can have several backs.
**Edge marks:** a notch or a pill on the top or bottom edge shows the front piece’s color through the back. A notched front fits only a notched back.
**The seam:** a thin line runs around the back, about 1.45 mm in from the edge.

items.text: **Solid:** one piece. The print pauses for you to drop the sticker in, and the rest of the card seals it inside.

Holders
the 3-card pocket case and the 5-card pocket case, open; the cards-only box, open

items.text: **Pocket cases,** for 3 or 5 cards. A drawer slides out of a branded sleeve, holding your cards plus a premium coin and a premium tag (see Fobs).
**The cards-only box** (the one on our table) has three bays: 10 finished cards, 4 loose fronts and 6 loose backs, for mixing and matching. It sits under a lid that carries the wordmark.

blocks.text: We made the holders for the booth. Their print files aren’t published.
How to get one

items.text: **Print your own.** Click **Customize** on MakerWorld (MAKERWORLD-CARD-URL), type your name, your link and your back’s lines, pick a theme, and download the 3MF. Or open the model in OpenSCAD’s Customizer from [github.com/tbutman/tilde-card](https://github.com/tbutman/tilde-card). The printing guide below has the rest. `[depends on U3]` for MakerWorld. `[depends on the card release]` for “pick a theme” and the GitHub model.

**Add an NFC sticker** if you want people to tap it: a round NTAG215, 22–25 mm across. Write it before it goes in, with Tilde (Android: Cards → Write a sticker `[depends on 1.3.0]`) or the free NFC Tools app (iPhone and Android).
**Get the app,** if you like. Tilde is free for Android: your phone becomes the same card. The printed card works without it.
